raw_segments.text: The tendencies, which I have just alluded to, are as yet very slightly perceptible in
political society, but they already begin to exercise an unfavorable influence upon
the national character of the Americans.
I am inclined to attribute the singular paucity of distinguished political characters to the
ever-increasing activity of the despotism of the majority in the United States.
When the American Revolution broke out they arose in great numbers, for public opinion
then served, not to tyrannize over, but to direct the exertions of individuals.
Those celebrated men took a full part in the general agitation of mind common at that
period, and they attained a high degree of personal fame, which was reflected back upon
the nation, but which was by no means borrowed from it.
